Quick start

How to use this tool

  1. Choose the common GPA scale used for both records.
  2. Enter your previous GPA and the GPA-bearing credits it covers.
  3. Enter a new, separate semester GPA and its GPA-bearing credits, then calculate.

See the formula ↓

How the calculation works

Cumulative GPA = (Previous GPA × Previous credits + New GPA × New credits) ÷ (Previous credits + New credits)

A worked example

A previous 3.20 GPA across 45 credits contributes 144 quality points. A new 3.80 GPA across 15 credits contributes 57. The combined estimate is (144 + 57) ÷ 60 = 3.35. Simply averaging 3.20 and 3.80 would incorrectly give 3.50.

Before you use the result

The result is an estimate if either input GPA was already rounded. For the closest match to a transcript, use full-precision quality points and institution rules. This calculator combines non-overlapping records only; it does not replace failed courses, reconcile different scales, or mix semester and quarter credits. Calculate the new term from individual courses using the semester GPA tool first if needed.

Results display to two decimal places unless stated otherwise. Read our calculation methodology for scope and limitations.

Frequently asked questions

Why can’t I average two GPAs directly?

Different credit totals carry different weight. A 45-credit record contributes three times as much as a 15-credit term.

What if my previous GPA includes this semester?

Do not enter that semester again. Use non-overlapping records or calculate from the underlying courses.

Does this apply grade forgiveness?

No. Retakes and grade replacement require your institution’s specific policy. Adjust the underlying record only if that policy permits it.
